reference.title: Scenario 1: Title metadata is present
reference.shortdesc: Consider an index .md file titled “Kubernetes User Documentation” in a folder named Kubernetes_user_doc.

section.p: Consider an index .md file titled “Kubernetes User Documentation” in a folder named Kubernetes_user_doc. When the prolog/header metadata of this file includes title = " Kubernetes User Documentation ", the converter generates the following DITA bookmap structure:

entry.codeblock: Folder: kubernetes_user_doc Filename: index.md +++ title = "Kubernetes User Documentation" description = "Kubernetes Operations and Management" type="page" weight = 180 +++ # User Documentation

<map id="kubernetes_user_doc"> <title> Kubernetes User Documentation</title> </map> OR <bookmap id="kubernetes_user_doc"> <booktitle> <mainbooktitle> Kubernetes User Documentation </mainbooktitle> </booktitle> </bookmap>

section.p: Result: The converter uses the folder name as the map @id. The title metadata in the prolog/header becomes the DITA map title. Use <map>/<title> for a standard DITA map, or <bookmap>/<booktitle>/<mainbooktitle> only when the target DITA shell supports bookmap.
